gotchas.gotcha: Commands are NOT protected by unified-creator-guard.cjs (unlike skills, agents, hooks, templates)
gotchas.why_it_happens: Commands are passive markdown prompts with no privilege escalation or integration coupling. Security threat model is equivalent to direct user input. Creator guard overhead not justified.
gotchas.trigger: Developers may expect commands to require skill-creator workflow
gotchas.solution: Commands are user-controlled, lightweight artifacts. Direct writes to .claude/commands/ are intentional and safe. No creator workflow required.
gotchas.alternatives_considered: Protect commands with creator-guard (rejected - adds complexity without proportional security benefit)
gotchas.extracted_from: Task #86 security compliance check, confirmed by Task #83 architecture design

gotchas.gotcha: While thin delegators (3-line shims) are scalable, they can become boilerplate at scale
gotchas.context: Commands System now has 16 identical 3-line delegators (only skill name varies)
gotchas.why_it_happens: Pattern is so simple that adding 1 command requires copy-paste of 3 lines
gotchas.trigger: After 10+ similar delegators are created manually, developers may want to automate
gotchas.solution: For future command additions: consider creating a command generator script or template expansion tool. But don't overcomplicate - 3-line pattern is maintainable
gotchas.future_enhancement: Optional: command-generator.cjs that takes skill name and generates command file

gotchas.gotcha: Enriched commands (/learn that integrates multiple features) can become maintenance burden if overused
gotchas.context: Only /learn enriches beyond single-skill delegation (combines context-compressor + memory protocol)
gotchas.why_it_happens: Developers may want to add convenience commands that combine multiple skills
gotchas.solution: Keep enriched commands rare. Document each enriched command's integration strategy in the catalog. Prefer orchestrating workflows via agent-level task chaining over command-level combinations.
gotchas.pattern: Enriched = single command + documentation of integration. Multi-step = agent delegation.
gotchas.extracted_from: Task #85 catalog design (1 enriched command documented as exception)

gotchas.gotcha: When moving files deeper in directory tree, __dirname-based path calculations must be updated
gotchas.context: Tools System Overhaul Phase C (Task #95) - relocated 8 modules from tools/ to lib/subdirs/
gotchas.why_it_happens: Code computes PROJECT_ROOT using relative paths like resolve(__dirname, '../..'). When file moves from depth 2 (tools/) to depth 3 (lib/workflow/), the depth changes.
gotchas.symptoms: Silent failures when computing PROJECT_ROOT - file operations target wrong directory, config files not found, MODULE_NOT_FOUND for sibling modules
gotchas.trigger: Relocating files from shallow to deep directory (or vice versa) without updating __dirname calculations
gotchas.detection_pattern: Search relocated files for __dirname, verify '../..' count matches new depth
gotchas.solution: Update all __dirname-based paths: resolve(__dirname, '../..') → resolve(__dirname, '../../..'). Better: use helper function that walks up to find .claude/CLAUDE.md
gotchas.example: Moved decision-handler.mjs from tools/workflow/ (depth 2) to lib/workflow/ (depth 3). Required updating resolve(__dirname, '../..') to resolve(__dirname, '../../..')
gotchas.prevention: Create computeProjectRoot() helper that walks directory tree instead of hardcoding depth
gotchas.extracted_from: Task #95 learnings.md, documented in ADR-089 implementation notes

gotchas.gotcha: Security scanner triggers false positives on test files containing intentional malicious strings
gotchas.context: Tools System Overhaul Phase C (Task #95) - decision-handler-security.test.cjs contains malicious expressions for testing
gotchas.why_it_happens: security-lint.cjs scans ALL .js/.cjs/.mjs files for dangerous patterns (eval, new Function, exec). Test files that verify these patterns are rejected correctly contain the patterns themselves.
gotchas.symptoms: security-lint.cjs fails on test files with ERROR: 'eval detected' or 'new Function detected' even though usage is safe (inside test strings)
gotchas.trigger: Creating security tests that include malicious code samples as test data
gotchas.solution: Add '// security-lint-ignore: Security test file - contains intentional malicious strings for validation' as first line of test file. Scanner skips files with this directive.
gotchas.example: decision-handler-security.test.cjs has malicious expression strings like 'process.exit(1)' and 'require("fs")' for testing parser rejection
alternatives: Extend security-lint.cjs to auto-detect test files (path includes tests/ or *.test.*)
Store malicious test data in separate .json file outside scan scope
Configure security-lint.cjs to allow eval/Function in test files only
gotchas.best_practice: Always include reason in ignore directive: // security-lint-ignore: <clear explanation>
